4 KiB pages read (read LPNs).
4 KiB pages written (write LPNs).
LeaFTL: written pages that replaced a page still in its 2,048-page write buffer, so only the newer one reaches flash (blank for LearnedFTL, which has no such buffer).
LeaFTL: written pages silently discarded by the buffer duplicate check (KI-27, a bug).
CMT hits on the read path (the FTL's own counter).
CMT misses on the read path (the FTL's own counter).

cmt_hits / (cmt_hits + cmt_misses); blank when there were no lookups. The FTL's own definition, including lookups for never-written pages; a LeaFTL entry covers a translation page, a LearnedFTL entry one page, so it is not comparable across FTLs: compare tp_reads_per_read_page instead.
CMT hits among served reads of written data / served reads (the same column as in baseline_summary.csv); the hit rate gap_to_belady is measured from.

LRU hit rate of an 8,192-entry cache on the trace's read stream, computed offline (experiments/tools/cachesim.c), keyed like the FTL's entries: per 256-page translation page for LeaFTL, per page for LearnedFTL. Counted per page, so pages of one request that follow its first page mostly hit.

Belady-OPT (a cache that knows the future) on the same stream and keying: the best any replacement policy can do with 8,192 entries filled on read misses, over all read pages. It bounds LeaFTL's hit rate over all lookups (cmt_hit_rate), not cmt_hit_rate_mapped, which covers served reads only. LearnedFTL also fills its cache on writes and prefetches the rest of each request, so it can exceed it.

LeaFTL only: bound_belady_hit_rate_8192 - cmt_hit_rate_mapped. Understates the gap, because lost reads (always cache misses) are left out of cmt_hit_rate_mapped; it can be negative. Blank for LearnedFTL (no valid bound).
LeaFTL only: bound_belady_hit_rate_8192 - cmt_hit_rate, both over (nearly) all read pages. Includes the effect of LeaFTL's lost reads and of caching only accurate segments. Blank for LearnedFTL.
Flash reads of user data (incl. reads of a mispredicted page).
Flash reads of translation pages, all causes.
Flash reads of valid data copied by garbage collection.
All flash reads: user + translation + GC.
Flash programs of host data.
Flash programs of translation pages (always 0 for LearnedFTL: not charged, KI-25).
Flash programs of GC-migrated data (always 0 for LeaFTL: not programmed, KI-22).
All flash programs: user + translation + GC.
Block erases.
Flash reads (user + translation) issued while the FTL was serving a read request.
All other flash reads: write requests, buffer flushes and GC (a GC started inside a read, possible for LearnedFTL, is counted here).
Translation-page reads issued while serving read requests (the reads the CMT exists to avoid): nand_reads_during_reads - nand_reads_user.
Translation-page reads outside read requests (map updates on writes and flushes, GC).
nand_reads_during_reads / read_requests. All read columns are blank for traces with no reads.
nand_reads_during_reads / read_pages. Over all read pages, incl. pages the FTL failed to resolve (see lost_data_read_share).
tp_reads_during_reads / read_requests.
tp_reads_during_reads / read_pages. Comparable across FTLs; 0 is ideal.
nand_reads_outside_reads / write_requests. All write columns are blank for traces with no writes.
nand_reads_outside_reads / write_pages.
tp_reads_outside_reads / write_requests.
tp_reads_outside_reads / write_pages.
nand_writes_total / write_requests.
nand_writes_total / write_pages (= WAF). Below 1 for LeaFTL when its buffer absorbs rewrites, drops writes (KI-27), or never fills (pages still buffered at the end are not programmed).

Reads of written data the FTL did not return / reads of written data (LeaFTL KI-27/KI-28); blank when no read targeted written data. Quote with LeaFTL's per-read costs: a lost read costs a translation read but no data read, which lowers those averages.
Caveats for this row, including why any field in it is blank.
